question_vi: Filter và HandlerInterceptor trong Spring khác nhau thế nào?
question_en: How do a Filter and a HandlerInterceptor differ in Spring?
answer_vi:
Cả hai chặn request trước controller, nhưng ở **tầng khác nhau**.

| | **Filter (Servlet)** | **HandlerInterceptor (Spring MVC)** |
|---|---|---|
| Tầng | Servlet container (trước DispatcherServlet) | Bên trong DispatcherServlet |
| Biết controller xử lý? | Không — Chưa | Có — Có (`handler` argument) |
| Truy cập Spring context | Hạn chế | Có — Đầy đủ (là Spring bean) |
| Sửa request/response body | Có — (wrap stream) | Không — Khó |
| Use case | CORS, gzip, security (Spring Security là filter), logging thô | Auth theo handler, đo thời gian xử lý, set attribute cho view |

**Cách viết:**
- **Filter:** extend `OncePerRequestFilter`, override `doFilterInternal(req, res, chain)` — nhớ gọi `chain.doFilter(...)` để request đi tiếp; đăng ký như `@Component`.
- **Interceptor:** implement `HandlerInterceptor` — `preHandle` trả `false` → chặn request, không tới controller; `postHandle` sau controller; `afterCompletion` sau cùng (kể cả khi exception). Đăng ký qua `WebMvcConfigurer.addInterceptors(...).addPathPatterns("/api/**")`.

**Chọn:** xử lý sớm/thô (security, CORS, nén, sửa body) → Filter; cần biết handler nào xử lý hoặc dùng Spring bean → Interceptor
answer_en:
Both intercept requests before the controller, but at **different layers**.

| | **Filter (Servlet)** | **HandlerInterceptor (Spring MVC)** |
|---|---|---|
| Layer | Servlet container (before DispatcherServlet) | Inside DispatcherServlet |
| Knows the handling controller? | No — Not yet | Yes — Yes (`handler` argument) |
| Access to Spring context | Limited | Yes — Full (it is a Spring bean) |
| Modify request/response body | Yes — (wrap streams) | No — Hard |
| Use case | CORS, gzip, security (Spring Security is a filter), raw logging | Per-handler auth, timing, view attributes |

**How to write them:**
- **Filter:** extend `OncePerRequestFilter`, override `doFilterInternal(req, res, chain)` — remember to call `chain.doFilter(...)` to continue; register as a `@Component`.
- **Interceptor:** implement `HandlerInterceptor` — `preHandle` returning `false` → blocks the request before the controller; `postHandle` after the controller; `afterCompletion` at the very end (even on exceptions). Register via `WebMvcConfigurer.addInterceptors(...).addPathPatterns("/api/**")`.

**Choose:** early/raw processing (security, CORS, compression, body rewriting) → Filter; need to know the handler or use Spring beans → Interceptor
